turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on he, she and it with -s?
turns.tutor:
Sure! Let me solve one example first and explain each step.
Sentence: "I read the news." Now change "I" to "she".
Step 1: "She" is one person, not me or you.
Step 2: So the verb needs -s: "She reads the news."
That is the rule: after he, she or it, add -s to the verb.
Right: He cooks dinner every evening. Wrong: He cook dinner every evening.

Now you try. Write only the verb:
Write the correct form: My sister ___ (play) tennis on Sundays. (answer with only the verb)

Rule: after he, she or it, add -s or -es to the verb.
